text.p: All divisions of Queensland's new megabank formed from the merger of Metway Bank Ltd, Suncorp and Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) were trading well in the current year, the bank's new chief executive said.
"We're having a very good (current) year. All three pieces of the business are performing very well," managing director Steve Jones told his first press conference.
"We're travelling very well and market share is holding up," Jones, formerly head of ANZ Bank's New Zealand operations, said.

Jones, who takes up his appointment on January 7, said the three divisions were doing "better than one might expect, given the uncertaintly that naturally comes in the staff's mind when something like this (the merger) goes through".
"If you look at the results, you wouldn't know you'd been through this process," he said.
Jones also said the new bank would have a new name by February - "what we're trying to do is find a strategic brand name to use as an umbrella over our products".
He declined to reveal his salary package or whether an option scheme for himself had been arranged.
"My expectation is that senior executives would all participate in the success - if not stock options, then other means," Jones said.
"I've discussed that with the selection commitee," he said.
Jones said the new bank would not be expanding outside Queensland in the next year.
"We've got beachheads outside Queensland -- we see them as beachheads only."
